lead: Obstetric cholestasis is itching without a rash with raised bile acids and/or abnormal liver tests and no other cause, usually in the third trimester, that resolves after birth. The mother itches; the fetus is at risk of sudden death.
f: Family history in 1 of 3, previous cholestasis, South Asian origin, twins · Pruritus of the palms and soles, then trunk; worse at night · Only scratch marks on examination; mild jaundice in a few; dark urine, pale stool, steatorrhoea

sc: Itchy palms and soles, no rash, bile acids raised → Obstetric cholestasis

f: Bile acids ≥ 19 µmol/L on a random sample (RCOG 2022): the key test; ≥ 100 = high fetal risk · ALT, AST, GGT 2–3 times normal; ALP not useful (placental) · PT for vitamin K deficiency · Exclude others: liver ultrasound, viral serology, autoantibodies · Itching with normal tests: repeat in 1–2 wk (itch can precede abnormal tests)

sc: 32 wk, itchy at night, normal LFT and bile acids → Repeat LFT and bile acids in 1–2 wk

f: Itch with a rash: eczema, scabies, polymorphic eruption, pemphigoid gestationis (blisters around the umbilicus) · Abnormal LFT: HELLP (BP, platelets), AFLP (vomiting, low glucose), viral hepatitis, gallstones, PBC (AMA), autoimmune hepatitis (ASMA)

sc: High ALP only, no itch at 34 wk → Normal (placental ALP)

f: Mother: itch, poor sleep, vitamin K deficiency → PPH; no lasting liver damage · Fetus: sudden stillbirth (risk rises with bile acids ≥ 100), meconium, preterm birth, neonatal respiratory distress

tr: A normal CTG does not exclude sudden fetal death in cholestasis: plan birth by the bile acid level

f: Ursodeoxycholic acid 8–12 mg/kg/day in 2 doses: itch improves in 1–7 days; no proven fetal benefit · Vitamin K (menadiol 10 mg daily) only if PT prolonged or steatorrhoea (RCOG 2022) · Emollients (aqueous cream with menthol); chlorphenamine only helps sleep · LFT and bile acids weekly; the peak level sets the birth timing

Peak bile acids 19–39: by 40 wk · 40–99: at 38–39 wk · ≥ 100: at 35–36 wk · Induction; CS for usual obstetric reasons; steroids if before 35 wk · Continuous CTG, active third stage · Local practice: fasting bile acids over 10, birth at 39 or 38 wk, vitamin K for all

sc: Bile acids 25 µmol/L at 34 wk → UDCA, birth by 40 wk
Bile acids 130 µmol/L at 34 wk → Plan birth at 35–36 wk

f: Itch goes within days; check LFT before discharge or at 6 wk · Still abnormal: look for chronic liver disease · Recurs in 45–70% of later pregnancies · Avoid oestrogen pills: use progestogen-only or IUCD
